paragraphs: Friend, here's what gets me about Absalom. Nothing he did on that road looked like a crime. A chariot, a handshake, a kiss, a kind word about your case. But the Bible says that in this way he "stole the hearts of the men of Israel" (2 Samuel 15:6). Theft doesn't always kick the door in. Sometimes it walks up smiling and tells you exactly what you want to hear.

Notice what he sold, too. He told people their claims were good and right, but "the king has no deputy to hear you" (2 Samuel 15:3). He pointed at a gap and made himself the answer. Then he took a vow to the LORD to Hebron, and it turned out to be the cover for a conspiracy (2 Samuel 15:7-10). I think that's the warning for us: holy-sounding words and a warm face don't prove a heart is honest. Even the two hundred guests who "went along innocently" (2 Samuel 15:11) show how easily good people get swept along when nobody checks.

So how do I, a worn-out stamper, bake this into my life? I weigh what people say against the Word, not against how nice they were to me. And I stay a faithful baker where I'm planted, because hearts get stolen when they go unwatched. The conspiracy is gaining strength, and this story is FAR from over, friend.
